thread.title_full: Multiple victims, including 2 police officers, in downtown Minneapolis shooting - NewsBreak

author: Joe Nelson
title: Multiple victims, including 2 police officers, in downtown Minneapolis shooting - NewsBreak
text:
By Joe Nelson ,
9 hours ago Three people are dead, including the suspect, and six others were injured in a mass shooting Wednesday at a downtown Minneapolis high-rise apartment complex.
Two of those wounded in the shooting are Minneapolis police officers, according to the city. A third officer was injured in the incident, but not by gunfire.
The shooting unfolded at 15 E Grant St. just after 4:30 p.m. at the Shoreline Plaza, formerly known as the Loring Towers.
A massive law enforcement response heavily impacted the downtown area at rush hour, but the city said the scene is secure as of 7:45 p.m. and there is no further threat to the public.
7: 30 p.m. – 3 dead, 3 officers taken to hospital The City of Minneapolis said that police were initially responding to reports of gunfire and information that one person had been shot.
Inside the apartment building, police encountered victims and followed the sound of additional gunfire to an upper floor where they “encountered a haze that significantly limited their visibility.”
The city said three officers were injured, two of them by gunfire. All were taken to Hennepin Healthcare and one officer is undergoing surgery.
“The suspected shooter is deceased, and one other person died at the scene,” the city shared. “Seven others were transported to Hennepin Healthcare. One of them died at the hospital.”
6:46 p.m. — BCA on scene, tactical unit exits building Izzy Canizares reports that Minnesota Bureau of Criminal Apprehension investigators are entering the Shoreline Plaza, while the MPD tactical unit appeared to be exiting the building.
6:21 p.m. — 7 total victims, 1 confirmed dead Hennepin Healthcare confirms that it received seven patients from the shooting and that one of the seven has died. The conditions of the six others haven’t been disclosed.
The shooter is reportedly dead, though police have yet to confirm as much.
6:15 p.m. — Tactical unit at Shoreline Plaz Izzy Canizares is at the scene for Bring Me The News and reports that Marquette Place and Shoreline Plaza are taped off and that the bulk of the police activity is at Shoreline Plaza.
“There is a tactical group looking to be going in right now. Everything is blocked off,” Canizares said. “They’re telling us to keep behind the line, so I’m not sure if the situation is clear or not.”
5:55 p.m. — FBI offers support 5:38 p.m. — Number of victims unconfirmed City officials say there are multiple victims, while KSTP-TV is reporting that at least six people, including the two officers, have been shot, and multiple civilians are dead.
The Minnesota Star Tribune, citing two sources familiar with the investigation, reports that the officers were shot on an upper floor of an apartment. One was reportedly struck in the chin and leg, and the other officer was shot in the stomach.
5:30 p.m. — Active shooter alert An active shooter alert was sent to people in the area just before 5:30 p.m., although the Star Tribune, citing unconfirmed dispatch audio, is reporting that the shooter is down.
5:15 p.m. — Crash involving police cruiser nearby Photos from downtown also show police activity near the Nicollet Mall Target, which is located less than a mile from the Loring Towers. In the images provided to Bring Me The News, there appears to be a sedan with front-end damage in the intersection, and a police cruiser with significant rear-end damage.
It’s unclear if the apparent crash is related to the shooting, although unconfirmed reports suggest that the crash happened while an officer was en route to the scene.

5:11 p.m. — Walz aware of the incident “My public safety team is responding to a shooting that took place downtown Minneapolis this afternoon. State officials are on the ground to support local law enforcement and we will share more information as it becomes available,” Gov. Tim Walz said.
“Grateful to law enforcement actively working to ensure the safety of our neighbors in Downtown Minneapolis this afternoon,” Walz added in a separate social media post. “Minnesota is praying for our first responders.”
This is a developing story.
summary: 6 hours ago Three people are dead, including the suspect, and six others were injured in a mass shooting Wednesday at a downtown Minneapolis high-rise apartment complex. A massive law enforcement response heavily impacted the downtown area at rush hour, but the city said the scene is secure as of 7:45 p.m. and there is no further threat to the public. 7: 30 p.m. – 3 dead, 3 officers taken to hospital The City of Minneapolis said that police were initially responding to reports of gunfire and information that one person had been shot.
